# How crawling errors affect Search

Day 1, 14:35 · Cherry Prommawin, Gary Illyes, Search Relations · coverage: notes, transcript

Cherry Prommawin presented the status codes and Gary Illyes the DNS, network, CDN and soft 404 errors (on-stage hand-overs; the host thanked both). Transcript from a second attendee recording and a complete audio recording.

## Claims

- **[Stage]** DNS issues and firewalls are blind spots: Google does not know a firewall is blocking it, it only sees that requests fail.
  <br><sub>`D1-C069` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors), [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Extended by [D1-C359](../day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extended by [D2-C374](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-04`, `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google treats network timeouts, connection resets and DNS errors like 5xx server errors: crawling slows down immediately, and already indexed URLs that stay unreachable are removed from Google's index within days.
  > "Google treats network timeouts, connection reset, and DNS errors similarly to 5xx server errors."
  <br><sub>`D1-C126` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors) · Extended by [D3-C618](../day3/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-04`, `DEV-SRV-01`, `DEV-SRV-03`, `F-017`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Soft 404s were named as a crawl problem alongside DNS and firewall issues, and described as one of the biggest problems on the internet right now for crawling and showing up in Search.
  <br><sub>`D1-C070` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [Optimize your crawl budget](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget), [Troubleshoot Google Search crawling errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) · Extended by [D2-C334](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** 5xx and 429 responses prompt Google's crawlers to slow down temporarily. Already indexed URLs are preserved in the index for a while but eventually dropped.
  > "already indexed URLs are preserved in the index, but eventually dropped"
  <br><sub>`D1-C071` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-SRV-03`</sub>

- **[Docs]** 4xx status codes other than 429 have no effect on crawl rate.
  > "The 4xx status codes, except 429, have no effect on crawl rate."
  <br><sub>`D1-C072` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Repeated by [D1-C385](../day1/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-01`</sub>

- **[Docs]** A soft 404 is a page that returns a success code while its content looks like an error or an empty page. It is kept out of the index but continues to be crawled, wasting crawl budget.
  <br><sub>`D1-C073` · Google, Google Search Central · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [Optimize your crawl budget](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget), [Troubleshoot Google Search crawling errors](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/troubleshoot-crawling-errors) · Extended by [D2-C190](../day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C213](../day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Repeated by [D2-C264](../day2/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C291](../day2/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Repeated by [D2-C334](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Extended by [D2-C336](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Extended by [D2-C367](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C700](../day2/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-01`, the glossary term *Soft 404*</sub>

- **[Docs]** If robots.txt returns a 5xx error, Google stops crawling the site for the first 12 hours, then uses the cached copy for up to 30 days.
  <br><sub>`D1-C074` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [How Google interprets the robots.txt specification](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/robots-txt/robots-txt-spec) · Extended by [D2-C210](../day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-04`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** For temporary blocks return 503 or 429, never a 200 page with a captcha or error message, which becomes a soft 404 and can replace real content in the index. Verify Googlebot by reverse DNS, not by user agent.
  <br><sub>`D1-C078` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · Extended by [D2-C339](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Extended by [D2-C374](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C376](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-MON-04`, `DEV-SRV-02`, `DEV-SRV-03`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's page on verifying its crawlers says Googlebot and Google's other common crawlers resolve to crawl-*.googlebot.com or geo-crawl-*.geo.googlebot.com host names, special-case crawlers to rate-limited-proxy-*.google.com and user-triggered fetchers to *.gae.googleusercontent.com or google-proxy-*.google.com, and it publishes each group's IP ranges as JSON files such as common-crawlers.json and special-crawlers.json.
  <br><sub>`D1-C138` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [Verify requests from Google crawlers and fetchers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/verify-google-requests) · Used by `DEV-MON-04`, `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** HTTP status codes fall into five classes, 1xx informational, 2xx success, 3xx redirection, 4xx client error and 5xx server error, and each class affects crawling differently.
  <br><sub>`D1-C345` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by the glossary term *HTTP status code classes*</sub>

- **[Stage]** 1xx informational status codes, which only say that a request was received and more data is coming, have no meaning of their own for crawling.
  <br><sub>`D1-C346` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** When a crawler's request returns 200, the page, file or other resource that comes back is eligible for indexing.
  <br><sub>`D1-C347` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A 204 No Content response is not eligible for indexing, because the server confirms the request but returns no content to index.
  <br><sub>`D1-C348` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-ERR-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google follows 3xx redirects, permanent (301, 308) and temporary (302, 307), to the new location, and whether content gets indexed depends on what the redirect target returns.
  <br><sub>`D1-C349` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A 304 Not Modified response tells Google's crawler that the content has not changed since its last visit.
  <br><sub>`D1-C350` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-SRV-08`</sub>

- **[Stage]** 404 Not Found and 410 Gone both tell Google there is nothing at the URL, so the URL is not indexable.
  <br><sub>`D1-C351` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-ERR-01`, `DEV-SRV-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A 403 response tells Google's crawler it has no permission to see the requested content, so there is nothing for Google to index.
  <br><sub>`D1-C352` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-SRV-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** 429 Too Many Requests is the exception among 4xx codes: instead of meaning there is nothing at the URL, it tells Google's crawler to slow down, and Google slows its crawling.
  <br><sub>`D1-C353` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-SRV-03`, the glossary term *HTTP status code classes*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google slows crawling when a site returns 5xx errors, because a 5xx usually means the server, and often the whole site, cannot serve requests, and Google does not want to break the site.
  <br><sub>`D1-C354` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extended by [D3-C618](../day3/D3-S17-how-long-does-it-take-to.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A soft 404 is a 404 in disguise: the page returns 200 but its content says something like 'page not found', information the site should have sent as the HTTP status.
  <br><sub>`D1-C355` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · confirmed by Google docs · [Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en), [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Repeated by [D2-C334](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Used by `DEV-ERR-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Soft 404 pages are still crawled like normal pages; their bigger consequences are for indexing, and they also affect crawling.
  <br><sub>`D1-C356` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Cherry Prommawin) · consistent with Google docs · [Optimize your crawl budget](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawl-budget), [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Gary Illyes called DNS and network errors a very common issue on the internet nowadays, and DNS problems very pesky to debug.
  <br><sub>`D1-C357` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes)</sub>

- **[Stage]** DNS errors get a site removed from Google Search very aggressively, and Search Console alerts site owners to them.
  <br><sub>`D1-C358` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors), [Crawl Stats report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9679690?hl=en) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Most network errors happen somewhere between the site's origin server and Google's data centers, where they are invisible to both Google and the site owner; the way TCP networks work leaves no way to see what went wrong there.
  <br><sub>`D1-C359` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C069](../day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** When Search Console reports network errors, the first step Google recommends is to ask the hosting provider, or the CDN, whether they changed anything.
  <br><sub>`D1-C360` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Network timeouts are usually caused close to the site, very often by a firewall, a CDN, the hosting provider or the DNS provider, and Google has no visibility into them.
  <br><sub>`D1-C361` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors), [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Network errors and timeouts, like DNS errors, can get a site removed from Google Search and, with it, from every feature that depends on Search.
  <br><sub>`D1-C362` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors), [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** For DNS and network errors caused by a firewall or CDN, Google advises checking whether new firewall rules were set recently and otherwise asking in the CDN's forum, as Google itself cannot see or help with these errors.
  <br><sub>`D1-C363` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Debug network and DNS errors for Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/dns-network-errors), [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Used by `DEV-SRV-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** A rise in HTTP errors in crawl reports can come from a CDN throttling crawlers by injecting 429 or 503 responses on the network path between Google's crawler and the site.
  <br><sub>`D1-C364` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns) · Used by `DEV-SRV-02`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google has recently seen more 403 responses to its crawlers (described on stage as 'authentication required'); it treats them as client errors, technically equivalent to 404 or 410, and drops those pages from Search and its AI features.
  <br><sub>`D1-C365` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes), [Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en) · Extended by [D1-C509](../day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google treats a 402 Payment Required response as a 404 Not Found, because Googlebot cannot pay for content.
  > "402 will just mean 404 to us"
  <br><sub>`D1-C366` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Extended by [D1-C509](../day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-09`</sub>

- **[Stage]** CDN captcha challenges often return HTTP 200; Googlebot does not solve them and sees only content with a 200 status, which indexing then classifies as a soft 404, reported as an error in Search Console.
  <br><sub>`D1-C367` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · consistent with Google docs · [Crawling December: CDNs and crawling](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2024/12/crawling-december-cdns), [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Extended by [D1-C508](../day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extended by [D2-C374](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Extended by [D2-C375](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-SRV-02`, the glossary term *Soft 404*</sub>

- **[Stage]** Search Console's page indexing report breaks down the reasons why pages do or do not show in Search, and its categories help find patterns in how a site's content is crawled and served to Google's crawlers.
  <br><sub>`D1-C368` · Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search (Gary Illyes) · confirmed by Google docs · [Page indexing report](https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203?hl=en) · Extended by [D1-C508](../day1/D1-S06-how-crawling-errors-affect-search.md) · Extended by [D2-C717](../day2/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's status code page says that with a 204 No Content response Google receives no content and cannot process it, and that a 2xx page whose content is empty or an error message shows as a soft 404 in Search Console.
  <br><sub>`D1-C369` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-ERR-03`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's crawlers follow up to 10 redirect hops by default (some products' crawlers have other limits); content served by the redirecting URL is ignored and the final target's content is processed instead.
  > "Any content Google receives from the redirecting URL is ignored, and the final target URL's content is processed instead."
  <br><sub>`D1-C370` · Google · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search · is the documentation · [How HTTP status codes affect Google's crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/troubleshooting/http-status-codes) · Used by `DEV-CAN-01`, the glossary term *Redirect chain*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Day 1 said a CDN captcha page served with HTTP 200 becomes a soft 404, while Day 2 (D2-C374, D2-C375) said such challenge pages are hard to recognise as errors and can be clustered as duplicates; Google's CDN post describes both outcomes, and in both the real pages drop out of Search.
  <br><sub>`D1-C371` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Do not answer verified Googlebot with 401, 402 or 403, for example from a login wall, a paywall or a pay-per-crawl setup: Google treats them like 404 and drops the pages, and Google's status code page says not to use 401 or 403 to limit crawling; to slow crawling temporarily, return 429 or 503.
  <br><sub>`D1-C372` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 1, How crawling errors affect Search</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said soft 404s, like some other problem categories, are looked up in Search Console's page indexing report, while other crawl issues are debugged in the Crawl Stats report.

- **[Stage]** Google has seen an uptick in 402 Payment Required responses to its crawlers, an even more recent trend than the rise in 403 responses.
